Beállítom Az amerikai kormány két tagja is azon a megtévesztésre használt repülőgépen tartózkodott, amelyről titokban lecsempészték Donald Trump elnököt a törökországi NATO-csúcs után. Marco Rubio külügyminiszter és Scott Bessent pénzügyminiszter is azon a gépen maradt, amelyről mindenki azt hitte, hogy az az Air Force One, és nem szálltak át arra a repülőgépre, amellyel Trump valójában távozott – írta a BBC . Július 8-án Donald Trump amerikai elnök a két miniszter és a sajtó képviselőinek jelenlétében felszállt az Air Force One-ra az ankarai repülőtéren, ám mielőtt elindult volna a gép, az elnök elrejtőzött egy cateringautóban, és titokban átszállították egy katonai repülőgépre, hogy azzal tegye meg a Washingtonig vezető utat. A beszámolók szerint a gépcserére egy iráni fenyegetésről szóló jelentés miatt volt szükség. Az Air Force One elnevezés technikailag mindig azt a repülőgépet jelöli, amelyen az amerikai elnök éppen tartózkodik. Ebben az esetben azonban a különleges kialakítású Boeing–747-es elnöki gép megtartotta az Air Force One hívójelet, és egyfajta csaliként szolgált. Trump hétfő este újságíróknak elárulta , hogy a megtévesztésről szóló döntést az amerikai hadsereg és a titkosszolgálat hozta meg. „Azt akarták, hogy egy másik gépre szálljak” – mondta Trump. A biztonsági fenyegetés pontos formája továbbra sem ismert, az amerikai elnök erről nem közölt részleteket, csak annyit mondott, hogy „rengeteg fenyegetést kap”. „Minden olyan elnököt, akinek jelentős a szerepe, rengeteg fenyegetés ér” – tette hozzá. Amerikai sajtóhírek szerint a fenyegetés egy vállról indítható rakétavetőhöz kapcsolódott. A beszámolók szerint Irán tudhatott arról, hol tartózkodik Trump a NATO-csúcstalálkozó alatt, beleértve azt is, hogy a szálloda melyik emeletén kapott szobát. A New York Times névtelen tisztviselőkre hivatkozva azt írta, hogy valakit hordozható föld-levegő rakétával láttak a török fővárosban rendezett NATO-csúcs közelében. Az egyelőre nem világos, hogy a miniszterek és a többi tisztviselő, valamint a gépen dolgozó légierő-személyzet közül ki tudott a műveletről. A sajtó képviselői azt mondták, ők nem tudták, hogy egy csaligépen utaztak. A CBS News szerint Rubio és Bessent azért maradtak az első gépen, hogy biztosítsák az elnöki utódlási rend folytonosságát arra az esetre, ha Trumppal történne valami. Ha az amerikai elnök meghal vagy cselekvőképtelenné válik, akkor a hatalmat először J. D. Vance alelnök venné át, őt követné a képviselőház elnöke, majd a szenátus pro tempore elnöke. A külügyminiszter ezután következik a sorban, őt pedig a pénzügyminiszter követi. Az eredetileg Air Force One-ként azonosított gépen maradt többek között Stephen Miller, a Fehér Ház helyettes kabinetfőnöke, valamint Steven Cheung, a Fehér Ház kommunikációs igazgatója is. A második gépen, amely Trumpot elrepítette Ankarából, az amerikai sajtó beszámolói szerint Pete Hegseth védelmi miniszter is ott volt. Trumpot elkísérte továbbá Natalie Harp, az elnök végrehajtási asszisztense, Dan Scavino, a Fehér Ház helyettes kabinetfőnöke, valamint Walt Nauta, az Ovális Iroda műveleteinek igazgatója is. http://usa.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202608/10.text: Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Asia-Pacific Americas Europe Middle East Africa China-US China-Europe China-Japan China-Africa Home World China-CEEC cooperation opening doors Nation's modernization drive delivers inclusive benefits to other countries In 2008, as the global financial crisis unfolded, Greece suffered some of the worst fallout. Piraeus Port, the largest seaport in the country, reported a loss of 13 million euros ($15 million), with outdated facilities, scarce vessel calls and frequent dockworker strikes dragging its operations into a deep crisis. During this challenging period, when investors worldwide deemed Greece too risky, a Chinese company stepped forward. China COSCO Shipping secured a concession to operate two of Piraeus' container terminals. Eight years later, in 2016, COSCO acquired a majority stake in the port, officially taking over its management and operations. By bringing in expertise, investment and machinery, the Chinese company successfully breathed new life into the port. Far from replacing local staff, it created thousands of jobs for Greeks. Today, after years of restructuring, Piraeus stands as one of the busiest ports in the Mediterranean. Charalampos Aravantinos-Simonetos, a youth coordinator for international and European affairs in Greece's Syriza party, shared the story of solidarity and cooperation with a roomful of young political leaders from China and Central and Eastern European countries, or CEECs, in June during a forum held in Wuhan, Hubei province. The Chinese approach, he said, stands in stark contrast to those countries that invest solely for their own benefit and show little concern for local communities. The project has helped strengthen bilateral ties and allowed both sides to benefit through economic cooperation, he added. According to Piraeus' financial report, the port achieved record total revenue of 251 million euros in 2025, up 8.6 percent year-on-year. The turnaround of Piraeus Port, far from an isolated story, is a microcosm of the cooperation synergy between China and Central and Eastern European countries under the China-CEEC Cooperation mechanism. Launched in 2012, the mechanism is a trans-regional platform jointly initiated by both sides. Over the past 14 years, the parties have remained committed to the principles of equality, mutual benefit in cooperation, openness and inclusiveness against the backdrop of a fluid international landscape. Today, it has grown into a full-fledged mechanism, with deepening cooperation and a series of outcomes delivering tangible benefits to various parties. In Croatia, the Chinese-built Peljesac Bridge has reduced a three-hour detour to just a few minutes' drive. In Serbia, Chinese investment has revived a century-old steel plant from the brink of closure. In Skopje, the capital of North Macedonia, thousands of citizens commute every day on buses manufactured by Chinese company Yutong Bus. Such projects have "greatly facilitated local travel and daily commutes, injected robust momentum into industrialization and urbanization, and constantly improved people's well-being", said Xiang Yuanzheng, an official with the Chinese Commerce Ministry's European Department. Over the years, bilateral cooperation has moved beyond traditional fields such as mining and logistics into emerging sectors. Contemporary Amperex Technology and other Chinese battery makers have set up plants in Hungary, Slovakia and Poland, while Slovenian pharmaceutical company Krka Group has launched a joint venture with Ningbo Menovo Pharmaceutical in East China's Zhejiang province. From 2012 to 2025, trade between China and the CEECs registered an average annual growth rate of over 8 percent, hitting a record high of 1.09 trillion yuan ($161.5 billion) in 2025. In the first half of this year, two-way trade volume reached 580.1 billion yuan, up 11 percent year-on-year, according to the General Administration of Customs. For Petre Danci, a Romanian who studied at Capital University of Economics and Business in Beijing from 2011 to 2018, China's modernization drive delivers inclusive benefits to other countries, an approach he believes is underpinned by the country's deep-rooted commitment to openness, mutual benefit and shared progress. Citing the four great inventions of ancient China — papermaking, printing, the compass and gunpowder — Danci said that none of these transformative innovations changed the world by staying inside China. "They changed the world because they moved, because they were shared, because people who never met the inventors gained access to the tools and used them to build something entirely new," he said. During his years in China, Danci witnessed the country's modernization drive firsthand, epitomized by the rise of China's "new four great inventions" — high-speed rail, mobile payments, bike-sharing and e-commerce. "China does not just invent things; it deploys them at scale, and the results speak for themselves," he said, adding that such technological advancement "is changing the lives of hundreds of millions of people in real time" not just in China, but also in other countries. Drawing a parallel between past and present, Danci noted that just as ancient inventions connected the world through trade routes and shared knowledge, nations today are connected through people-to-people and technological exchanges across borders. "The cooperation between China and CEECs is a clear example of this connection," he said. Across the Eurasian region, this deepening connection has taken tangible shape. Irena Lukajic Korica, an adviser to the Office of the Serb Member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, said her country is among the top recipients of Chinese-backed infrastructure and energy projects in Central and Eastern Europe, with the total value of these projects reaching nearly 2 billion euros. Noting that China's remarkable pace of development — transforming itself into one of the world's leading economies within just a few decades — has won widespread recognition in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Korica said young people in her country embrace the joint pursuit of modernization of China and the CEECs as opportunities for mutual learning, cooperation and shared development. "They believe deeper cooperation can unlock new prospects in areas such as digital transformation, green energy, scientific research, tourism, cultural exchange and entrepreneurship," she said. "Young people across my country are interested in the educational opportunities that China offers," she added, noting that for them, "China is no longer a distant country, but a place where they can study, gain experience and better understand a different culture and development model." Michal Bartek, a member of the Slovak Parliament and deputy governor of Slovakia's Trencin region, said that every time he visits China, he brings back something unique. "China is really inspirational for us," he said. "You have achieved remarkable progress in national development, and I hope to introduce valuable experience to my region." Artificial intelligence can accelerate claims resolution Events Our Brands Outsourcing Today Automotive Today Sustainability Today Home Topics Finance tbi bank increases financing for Hexagon’s Someșului 15 project in Cluj-Napoca to... tbi bank increases financing for Hexagon’s Someșului 15 project in Cluj-Napoca to 15 million euros Finance Real estate News Latest News Published on September 2, 2026 By Petre Barac Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Email tbi bank is expanding its partnership with Hexagon by providing an additional 5 million euros in financing for the completion of the Someșului 15 project, one of the group’s premium residential developments in the central area of Cluj-Napoca. The new facility adds to the 10 million euros financing granted in 2025, bringing the total financing to 15 million euros. Someșului 15 is being developed in Cluj-Napoca city centre, near the Someș River, and comprises 136 apartments, commercial units and a two-level underground car park, across buildings with a height regime of two basement levels, ground floor and five/six upper floors. The project incorporates green areas and energy-efficient design solutions and is being developed by Hexagon, a group with many years of experience and a portfolio that includes major real estate projects. “In real estate, you are not simply financing square metres, but the confidence that a strong project will be successfully delivered. Our relationship with Hexagon has developed over time, and the additional financing for Someșului 15 is a natural step in a partnership built around experience, strong execution capabilities and a project that is highly relevant to a robust market such as Cluj-Napoca. For us, this is exactly the kind of development we want to support: well located, well executed and backed by a clear long-term perspective”, said Marius Constantinescu, Head of Business Banking Sales, tbi bank România. “Someșului 15 is an important project for us, both in terms of its location and concept, as well as the quality standards we have set for its development. tbi bank’s decision to increase the financing confirms the trust built over time. In a market where execution discipline matters more than ever, partnerships like this make the difference between a well-designed project and one that is successfully delivered”, said Florin Măriș, Fondator & CEO, Hexagon. The portfolio developed to date includes residential, retail and office projects in Cluj and Bucharest. At the beginning of 2026, tbi bank entered a new phase of development following its acquisition by Advent International, one of the world’s leading private equity investors, with approximately 100 billion US dollars in assets under management. https://www.foxnews.com/politics/kimberl.text: Kimberly Guilfoyle confirmed Tuesday that she is leaving her post as U.S. ambassador to Greece after the White House revealed on Tuesday that President Donald Trump had asked her to resign. Her departure follows a cascade of allegations in recent weeks, including that she sought help from a Trump donor to pay off a $100,000 credit card bill, offered access to senior administration officials, promoted the interests of a Greek company and mistreated embassy staff. The ambassador again denied the allegations that led to her ouster in a lengthy X post on Tuesday and pledged her continued loyalty to the president — who was almost her father-in-law. But Trump distanced himself from Guilfoyle on Tuesday even though his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., was engaged to her for four years. "Kimberly Guilfoyle — she was almost a member of your family. How surprised were you to learn about these allegations? What did you think?" a reporter asked Trump before he departed for Alaska. "She wasn't a member of my family. She, I guess, dated my son a long time ago," Trump shot back. "She was doing a good job, but we didn't like what we were reading." New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia announced during her first briefing to the press on Tuesday that Guilfoyle was asked to leave her post. "She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well," Zacharia said. It came one day after Trump publicly acknowledged that he was considering firing Guilfoyle. "Serving as the United States Ambassador to Greece has been the honor of a lifetime," Guilfoyle wrote in an X post confirming her ouster. "I will forever be grateful to President Donald J. Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio for entrusting me with the extraordinary privilege of representing the greatest country in the history of the world." Guilfoyle directly rejected the allegations involving her financial dealings, treatment of embassy staff and relationships with foreign business interests that have engulfed her tenure in recent weeks. "These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity," she wrote. "I will not allow false accusations to define my decades of public service." She did not directly address the White House's decision to ask her to resign or say when she would formally leave the post, but acknowledged that her tenure was ending. "While my time as Ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end," she wrote. She also stressed that her support for Trump remains unchanged. "My gratitude and respect for President Trump and Secretary Rubio remain unwavering," Guilfoyle wrote. "I am proud of what we accomplished together, and I will always be a loyal supporter of President Trump and his mission to Make America Great Again." TRUMP 'LOOKING AT' FIRING AMBASSADOR TO GREECE: 'WE'RE NOT HAPPY' Guilfoyle was with Donald Trump Jr. for six years, four of which they were engaged. They publicly split in December 2024, the same month Trump nominated her to serve as ambassador to Greece. The ambassador came under scrutiny last week after The Wall Street Journal reported that she asked Trump donor Eric Deters to pay off a $100,000 American Express bill shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing in July 2025. According to messages reviewed by the Journal, Guilfoyle urged Deters to wire the money directly to American Express, saying the transaction would not leave a paper trail, while offering to help him gain access to senior Trump administration officials. Deters said he never made the payment. Guilfoyle's attorney, Jesse Binnall, disputed the authenticity of the messages, saying Guilfoyle had been paid to speak at events before her nomination and "was owed a balance for traveling to and supporting these patriotic events." The allegations followed an earlier Journal investigation into Guilfoyle's conduct in Greece, including claims that she promoted the interests of Greek construction and energy company Aktor Group and allowed its registered lobbyist, Christos Marafatsos, to accompany her to private diplomatic meetings with senior officials. The Journal also reported that Guilfoyle suggested at a dinner with Greek officials that the U.S. would undermine their government, citing political developments in Romania. Greece's foreign minister subsequently said there was no need to summon Guilfoyle for an explanation because the country's energy minister denied that any threat had been made. Separately, the State Department's Office of Inspector General reportedly opened an investigation into allegations involving Guilfoyle's treatment of embassy employees, private travel, acceptance of gifts and relationships with business interests, according to the Daily Mail. HOUSE DEMOCRAT INVESTIGATED OVER ALLEGED 'INAPPROPRIATE SEXUAL CONTACT' WITH STAFFER Sources described a hostile workplace in which Guilfoyle allegedly threatened to fire employees. They also claimed that she demoted members of her security detail over minor incidents, including an officer who reportedly failed to answer a 4 a.m. request for ice while she was vacationing in Mykonos. The inspector general's office declined to confirm or deny the existence of an investigation. Binnall told the Daily Mail that "any implication of wrongdoing by the Ambassador is unsupported." The allegations drew scrutiny from congressional Democrats, including Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H., and Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., who called for a review of Guilfoyle's conduct. Meeks urged her removal if the allegations were substantiated. Vice President JD Vance addressed the controversy Friday, cautioning against rushing to judgment while acknowledging that misconduct should carry consequences. "Let's actually see what the facts are. Let's see what the truth is," Vance told reporters in Ohio. "And obviously, if there was something bad that happened, then people have to suffer consequences for it." Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who visited Greece last week and delivered remarks against the backdrop of the Acropolis, initially defended Guilfoyle's performance. "Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here," Rubio told reporters Wednesday. A day later, Rubio declined to address the allegations directly, challenging reporters over their reliance on unnamed sources. "You guys walk around thinking that because some source told you something, and you reported it, it's the gospel. It's not the gospel," Rubio said last Thursday. Just days later, the White House announced their request for her resignation. Trump nominated Guilfoyle to the diplomatic post in December 2024. A former California prosecutor and longtime Trump ally, she previously served as a prominent surrogate and fundraiser for the president.
